sections.title: Begin with a destination for the energy
paragraphs: A useful solar plan begins with a service you want: lower purchased electricity, an overnight refrigerator supply, or an independent workshop. These goals place different demands on the same energy source. Imagine following one unit of energy across a diagram. Sunlight reaches a module; cells produce electrical power; conversion equipment delivers it to a useful circuit; the energy is consumed, stored, exported, or lost as heat. Buying a larger array changes the first part of that journey without automatically changing every downstream limit.

A module is a manufactured assembly of cells. An array is a collection of modules. Balance of system means the remaining equipment and infrastructure needed to make the array useful. Treat these words as responsibilities rather than shopping categories. A complete project includes mounting, protection, controls, metering, permissions, and documentation. If a quotation only discusses module watts, ask who is responsible for the rest of the journey.

sections.title: Follow DC into AC without losing the boundary
paragraphs: Direct current, or DC, is the electrical form at a PV module and at a battery's terminals. Alternating current, or AC, serves ordinary household distribution. An inverter performs the conversion. Do not imagine that it simply changes a label: it has a finite power rating, efficiency, operating envelope, and control strategy. The inverter output is a useful measurement boundary because it tells you what generation is available to AC loads after that conversion.

Choose one boundary before balancing numbers. If you subtract an AC refrigerator demand from raw DC module output, you have silently ignored conversion loss. In a drawing, label each arrow DC or AC and locate the measuring device. A controller that charges a battery from PV and an inverter that serves AC loads may be separate boxes or parts of a combined product. The number of enclosures does not tell you which functions exist.

sections.title: Daylight: the system balances a changing budget
paragraphs: A load is anything consuming electrical power. Solar output and the sum of loads change throughout the day. At a single instant, production can cover some or all of demand. Surplus means production remaining after the selected loads at the same boundary. It can enter a battery, cross an approved export connection, or be curtailed. Curtailment means deliberately reducing available production because a limit or instruction prevents its use.

Self-consumption is generated energy used on site rather than exported. It is not a separate machine or a guarantee that all solar will stay inside the property. A home with an empty midday schedule may export heavily even if its annual consumption exceeds annual solar production. A full battery and a low export allowance can leave nowhere for additional power to go. That condition is an operating constraint, not necessarily a broken array.

sections.title: Work a sunny-hour energy balance
paragraphs: Keep this example deliberately simple so every number can be traced. All values below are at the AC household boundary; solar, demand, and battery charging remain constant for one hour. The assumed battery figure is power absorbed from that AC boundary, not energy added internally. Losses inside storage are excluded from this first balance and must be added when estimating later runtime.

Writing the balance before calculating prevents double counting. Production and grid import are sources; loads, battery charging, and export are destinations. If a destination cannot accept its assigned power, the controller must change another flow. A balance identifies the required behavior; only the actual equipment documentation establishes whether the behavior is supported.

workedExample.title: One hour with solar, loads, and charging
givens: AC solar output: 4.0 kW for one hour.
Household load: 1.5 kW; AC power entering battery charger: 1.0 kW.
Export is permitted; no other flows or changes.
steps: Allocate 1.0 kW to charging, leaving 1.5 kW for export.
Multiply each flow by one hour: 4.0 kWh generated = 1.5 kWh used + 1.0 kWh into charger + 1.5 kWh exported.
workedExample.result: The one-hour balance closes at 4.0 kWh.
workedExample.discussion: If charger-to-battery efficiency were an assumed 90%, internal stored energy would rise by only 0.9 kWh. The remaining 0.1 kWh is loss; it was already included in the charger input, so do not subtract it again from the AC balance.

sections.formula: Generation + import + battery discharge = loads + battery charging + export + boundary losses

sections.title: Nighttime changes supply, not the load's needs
paragraphs: At night there is no useful PV production in this elementary scenario. A grid-connected home can import electricity. A battery may discharge if the operating mode, state of charge, and reserve settings allow it. State of charge, abbreviated SOC, estimates how much charge remains relative to a defined capacity. A reserve is energy intentionally retained rather than spent on routine bill management. A dashboard's full battery icon does not explain how much reserve remains available to a particular circuit.

Distinguish energy from power here. A large energy store can still have a modest discharge power limit. A small load can run for a long time while a large load may exceed the inverter rating immediately. Describe backup in two sentences: which simultaneous loads must operate, and for how long under specified weather and starting charge. This is far more useful than asking for an unspecified whole-home battery.

sections.title: An outage is a different electrical state
paragraphs: Grid-following generation uses a grid reference. Supplying an isolated home requires equipment able to establish the local electrical conditions and a system that separates the backed-up circuits from the utility as required. DOE distinguishes grid-following and grid-forming functions. A battery's presence alone does not prove the complete installation has the transfer, controls, and approved architecture necessary for an outage.

Trace the outage path independently of the normal-operation path. Mark the loads that remain supported and identify any loads intentionally excluded. Ask what happens if the battery is depleted before sunrise, whether solar can restart the isolated system, and how transfer is demonstrated. Answers depend on the exact system. A daytime-only operating feature, a portable power station, and a permanent home backup installation should not be treated as interchangeable promises.

sections.title: Read the map as a reference table
paragraphs: Use the following table to organize a planning discussion. Its purpose is to associate a quantity with a question. It does not specify terminals or switching instructions. Every real installation needs a drawing that reflects its own conversion stages and measurement locations.

If two people report different production totals, compare their boundaries before deciding that either meter is wrong. Module output, inverter output, and utility export are different quantities. Export excludes generation already used by the home. Battery cycling can add further differences between the energy generated today and the energy consumed today.
rows: Generation available on the AC side
Import and export at the service boundary
Energy withheld by an operating setting

sections.title: Diagnose the story and check understanding
paragraphs: The common mistake is treating solar capacity, storage capacity, and backup capability as one specification. A system can have ample yearly generation and still fail an overnight objective. Another mistake is assuming that export is wasted energy in every tariff; export value belongs to the actual utility arrangement. Diagnose a disappointing result by asking which condition changed: sunlight, load, reserve, an equipment limit, or the permitted grid interaction.

Write a project brief that includes an operating state and an observable result. For example: keep a specified refrigerator and communications equipment running for twelve hours after a sunset outage from a stated starting charge. Then draw the normal and outage energy paths. Missing arrows become questions for the designer, and the finished brief becomes the basis of a handover demonstration.

exercise.question: Solar delivers 3 kW AC while loads draw 2 kW. The battery charger accepts 0.5 kW AC. What export is needed to close the balance, and what happens if export is prohibited?
exercise.answer: Required export is 0.5 kW. With export prohibited, some flow must change: generation must be reduced or another allowed destination must accept the surplus.
exercise.explanation: At the common AC boundary, 3 − 2 − 0.5 = 0.5 kW remains. Energy conservation identifies the surplus but does not establish which control action a particular product can perform.

solar-energy-path.outcome: Explain the energy balance during daylight, nighttime, and an outage, and translate a project goal into a testable operating requirement.

sections.title: Give every number a quantity and a location
paragraphs: An electrical number becomes meaningful only when it has a unit, location, and condition. A label reading 48 V may describe a nominal battery class; a reading of 48 V may describe the measured terminal voltage under a particular load. They are not interchangeable statements. Nominal means a convenient identifying value. Rated means a value assigned under stated operating conditions. Measured means a value observed with an instrument and its limitations.

Voltage, measured in volts, expresses electrical potential difference. Current, measured in amperes, describes charge flow. Power, measured in watts, describes the rate of energy transfer. Energy, measured in watt-hours or kilowatt-hours, accumulates over time. Resistance, measured in ohms, relates voltage drop to current in a resistive element. These terms form the grammar of a design conversation: leaving out a unit is like leaving out the subject of a sentence.

figures.caption: Series and parallel connections change different electrical quantities. The drawing is a conceptual comparison.
figures.alt: Two conceptual circuits show voltage adding in series and current adding in parallel.

sections.title: Power is a rate; energy is an accumulation
paragraphs: A 1,000 W heater draws 1 kW while operating. If it operates continuously for three hours, it consumes 3 kWh. If a thermostat operates it for fifteen minutes during each hour, its three-hour energy is 0.75 kWh under that assumed pattern. The duty cycle is the fraction of time a device operates. A label's rated power does not reveal the duty cycle of a refrigerator or the intensity settings of an appliance.

When power varies, calculate energy by adding each interval's power multiplied by its duration. A graph makes this intuitive: energy is the area under the power curve. Be careful with interval-average readings. A quarter-hour average may be useful for energy but can conceal a brief starting surge. Write both the energy budget and the simultaneous power requirement when assessing an inverter and battery.

figures.caption: Hypothetical loads: 2 kW for 3 hours and 6 kW for 1 hour both consume 6 kWh, while requiring different power capability.
figures.alt: Two power-versus-time rectangles have equal energy area: two kilowatts for three hours and six kilowatts for one hour.

sections.title: Use DC equations with honest assumptions
paragraphs: For a simple DC operating point, power is voltage multiplied by current. Ohm's law gives voltage drop across a resistance as current multiplied by resistance. Resistive heating is current squared multiplied by resistance. These equations explain why a low-voltage battery circuit can carry substantial current even when the load's wattage sounds modest. They also explain why a small unwanted connection resistance deserves attention.

An inverter is not an ideal wire. To estimate DC current from an AC load, divide the AC power by an assumed conversion efficiency and then by the actual battery voltage. The result is a screening estimate, not a cable or protection specification. Actual design also considers permissible current, installation conditions, fault interruption, surge behavior, terminal requirements, and applicable rules. Never substitute a nominal voltage when a conservative operating voltage is required.
sections.formula: DC power = V × I; voltage drop = I × R; resistive loss = I² × R

sections.title: Work through a battery-to-load calculation
paragraphs: The worked example separates a real load from its upstream demand. Its values are hypothetical and deliberately round. The efficiency is a chosen calculation input rather than a claim about a particular inverter. Treat the specified cable resistance as the total path resistance, including outgoing and return conductors; otherwise the voltage-drop calculation would be incomplete.

Results can be checked two ways. The resistive loss follows from current squared times resistance, and it also equals current times the resulting voltage drop. Small differences arise from rounding and from treating current as fixed despite the small loss. For preliminary teaching this is acceptable; a detailed design uses the equipment's operating range and more precise assumptions.

workedExample.title: A 960 W AC load on a battery system
givens: AC load: 960 W; assumed inverter efficiency: 90%.
Battery operating voltage for the estimate: 48 V.
Total DC conductor-path resistance: 0.020 Ω; ignore other losses.
workedExample.result: The simplified battery current is about 22.2 A and the conductor path dissipates about 9.9 W.
workedExample.discussion: The 0.444 V drop is approximately 0.93% of 48 V. This percentage is an arithmetic result, not an installation acceptance criterion. Including the loss in a more exact source-current calculation would increase current slightly.

sections.title: AC introduces apparent power and power factor
paragraphs: In a single-phase AC circuit, RMS voltage multiplied by RMS current gives apparent power in volt-amperes, or VA. RMS is the effective value used for these AC quantities. Real power in watts is the portion that transfers net energy to the load. Power factor is the ratio of real power to apparent power. A 600 W load at power factor 0.75 draws 800 VA; it does not become an 800 W energy consumer merely because its apparent power is larger.

An inverter can be constrained by both watts and VA, along with starting demands. This is why an appliance's watts alone may not settle compatibility. Do not assume a universal household power factor or motor surge multiplier. Obtain model information or suitable measurements. Three-phase systems require their own relationships and phase context; the single-phase equations in this chapter should not be stretched to cover every electrical service.
sections.formula: Single-phase apparent power S = Vrms × Irms; power factor = real power P ÷ S

sections.title: Read module boundary values correctly
paragraphs: Open-circuit voltage, Voc, is measured with no external load current. Short-circuit current, Isc, describes the short-circuit boundary. Maximum-power voltage, Vmp, and current, Imp, identify an operating point where their product is largest under the stated conditions. Voc and Isc do not occur simultaneously as the useful operating point, so multiplying them overstates the module's rated power.

A current-voltage curve, usually shortened to I-V curve, plots the possible current and voltage combinations under a condition. Standard test conditions provide a common laboratory comparison, not a forecast of every rooftop hour. Temperature and irradiance alter the curve. Keep the datasheet's coefficient units intact: a percentage change per degree must be divided by one hundred before use as a fractional multiplier. A negative voltage temperature coefficient means colder cells raise voltage relative to the reference.

figures.caption: Voc and Isc are opposite ends of an I-V curve; the useful maximum-power point lies between them.
figures.alt: An I-V curve labels short-circuit current, open-circuit voltage, and the maximum-power operating point.

sections.title: Keep battery charge and energy units distinct
paragraphs: An amp-hour is a quantity of electrical charge. Multiplying nominal volts by amp-hours gives an approximate nominal watt-hour value, useful for comparing battery classes. It does not establish usable delivered AC energy. Capacity conditions, operating limits, reserve, temperature, aging, and conversion change what a load can receive. A statement such as '100 Ah lasts ten hours' is incomplete unless the current and conditions are specified.

The following table is a translation aid. Use it to catch category errors before comparing products. A unit can be mathematically correct and still belong to the wrong measurement boundary: battery-terminal watt-hours are different from AC-delivered watt-hours. Preserve the original specification as well as any calculated value so another person can reconstruct the comparison.
rows: Potential difference or stated nominal system class
Operating or boundary current at a stated point
Battery charge capacity under stated conditions

sections.title: Diagnose unit errors and review the calculation
paragraphs: Common errors include writing kW per hour when you mean kWh, treating a daily energy total as a peak load, comparing batteries by amp-hours without voltage, and using module nameplate power as an hourly guarantee. Add a unit to every intermediate calculation. If the units do not cancel to the result you want, the formula is probably being applied incorrectly.

Precision should match evidence. A measured load averaging roughly 200 W over a few days does not justify a lifetime energy forecast to six decimal places. Keep unrounded values for arithmetic, but report appropriate precision and explain assumptions. The most useful number is the one whose meaning a future reviewer can recover, not the one with the longest string of digits.

exercise.question: A device uses 500 W real power at power factor 0.8 on an assumed 125 V RMS single-phase supply. It runs for two hours. Find apparent power, current, and energy.
exercise.explanation: S = 500 ÷ 0.8 = 625 VA; I = 625 ÷ 125 = 5 A; real energy = 0.5 kW × 2 h = 1 kWh. Apparent power is relevant to current and equipment capability; real power accumulates into this energy total.

sections.title: Draw functions before drawing product boxes
paragraphs: A product catalog divides a solar installation into modules, inverters, batteries, mounting parts, and accessories. A functional map asks different questions: who produces power, who converts it, who stores it, who controls it, who interrupts faults, who supports the structure, and who measures the result? This map prevents a combined enclosure from hiding a missing function and prevents several separate enclosures from being mistaken for needless duplication.

Start with the goal and the supply modes. A bill-reduction array and a selected-load backup system may share modules while needing very different conversion and control arrangements. Draw one box per function first. Only after the arrows make sense should you group functions into actual products. An integrated hybrid inverter might contain several functions, but its name does not prove every desired operating mode or every battery interface.

figures.caption: Compare central DC-to-AC conversion with conversion at each module. Storage and optimizers are separate functions and are not shown here.
figures.alt: PV modules feed one string inverter in a central example; individual modules feed microinverters and an AC branch in a module-level example.

sections.title: Generation and support form one physical assembly
paragraphs: The module transforms incident light into electrical power. Its mechanical dimensions, frame, mass, clamp requirements, connector system, and cable reach are as relevant to installation as its wattage. The mounting assembly transfers forces into a roof or foundation and maintains the intended orientation. A module that fits the roof geometrically may still fall outside the mounting system's supported mechanical configuration.

Think of the interface as a contract between components. One side describes allowed clamp zones and load conditions; the other specifies approved attachment and support geometry. The engineer or qualified designer reconciles them with the site. Do not assume that a generic rail, an arbitrary clamp, and a module of the right width form an approved assembly. Record exact part families so later substitutions can be reviewed coherently.

sections.title: Conversion and control answer different questions
paragraphs: An inverter converts DC to AC. Maximum power point tracking, or MPPT, adjusts the PV operating point to seek useful output under changing conditions. A solar charge controller regulates a PV-to-battery path. These jobs can coexist inside one product, but they should remain separate in your reasoning. A converter's efficiency describes a loss relationship; its control limits determine whether energy can flow at all.

The real Victron SmartSolar MPPT 150/35 is a helpful label-reading example, not a recommended home-grid architecture. Its manual distinguishes a 150 V maximum PV open-circuit limit from a 35 A maximum battery-current rating. The numbers concern different sides of the device. It is a solar charger; using it does not by itself establish AC household supply, export approval, or backup transfer. Model-specific context matters more than a memorable product name.

sections.title: Storage has an energy interface and a permission interface
paragraphs: A battery presents electrical terminals, but modern storage also has operating permissions. A battery management system, or BMS, supervises conditions and may limit or prohibit charging or discharge. The inverter or charger must respond through the arrangement supported by the equipment. A communication connector that physically fits does not prove protocol compatibility, firmware support, or the required cable pinout.

Usable energy, continuous power, and starting capability are separate specifications. Parallel batteries can change the bank's capability only within the manufacturer's allowed architecture. Describe each storage interface explicitly: allowable operating voltage, charge and discharge limits, communications or enable signals, environmental conditions, and the consequence of losing control. 'Both products say 48 V' answers only a small part of this compatibility problem.

sections.title: Protection, isolation, and grounding are functions too
paragraphs: An overcurrent protective device limits damage from specified excessive-current conditions. A disconnect provides an intended means of isolation. Grounding and bonding address different electrical relationships within a designed safety system. These are not ornamental accessories added after choosing the attractive boxes. Their ratings, placement, and coordination belong to the electrical design.

DC and AC devices have application-specific ratings. A device's current rating alone does not tell you whether it can interrupt the prospective fault or operate at the circuit's voltage. Battery fault conditions differ from PV source behavior. This chapter helps identify the missing information; it does not provide universal fuse sizes, bonding arrangements, or a switching sequence. Those decisions require the actual equipment, system architecture, and applicable installation requirements.

figures.caption: Protection and isolation belong on the functional map wherever the design requires them.
figures.alt: A conceptual DC path identifies source, conductors, overcurrent protection, disconnect, and conversion equipment.

sections.title: Work an interface map for a small hypothetical cabin
paragraphs: Suppose a cabin's essential AC appliances use 2.4 kWh per day, and the owner wants one sunless day of service. That objective identifies functions before products: daytime generation, charging regulation, stored energy, AC conversion, protected distribution, and a supported mounting arrangement. The calculation below is deliberately limited to an energy estimate. It does not settle starting demands, seasonal recovery, or installation compliance.

Notice that the resulting capacity is stated at a boundary. The hypothetical 80% operating window describes the portion of nominal storage made available by this scenario, and the assumed 90% conversion describes its delivery to AC loads. Neither is a universal battery recommendation. In the next design stage, replace these assumptions with the actual storage system's documented limits and verified operating behavior.

workedExample.title: Energy and conversion functions for one day
givens: Essential AC consumption: 2.4 kWh over one day.
Assumed usable battery window: 80% of nominal energy.
Assumed battery-to-AC delivery efficiency: 90%; no solar during the day.
steps: Separately list the simultaneous watts and starts; the 3.33 kWh figure does not determine inverter power.
Mark a charging function and a recovery-energy requirement for the next sunny period.
workedExample.result: The simplified energy estimate is 3.33 kWh nominal storage, with power and recovery still unresolved.
workedExample.discussion: If a second sunless day is required under the same assumptions, the energy estimate doubles. If a large motor cannot start, doubling stored energy may not solve the power-interface limitation.

sections.title: Use an interface register as the reference table
paragraphs: An interface register is a compact list of what must agree between two parts. Put a document reference beside each final value. The register is especially useful when comparing packages because sellers may omit different functions from similarly named kits. A package with modules and conversion equipment may still exclude attachments, conductors, metering, protected load distribution, or approval work.

Record uncertainty as a question with an owner. An unverified communications pair should remain unverified even if another brand's system looks similar. A register also helps a future technician: knowing the controller model and battery interface is far more useful than a receipt reading 'solar kit.' The table below is a starting structure, not a complete bill of materials.
rows: Voltage and current envelope; allowed string arrangement
Module datasheet and exact input specification
Approved battery pairing and control documentation
Supported service and authorized operating mode

sections.title: Diagnose a missing function and review
paragraphs: A common mistake is naming parts without identifying responsibilities. 'We have an inverter' does not establish charging, isolated operation, export limitation, or monitoring. Another mistake is thinking that an accessory omitted from the quotation can be chosen independently later. A sensor, control cable, or transfer component may be essential to the intended operating mode.

Revisit the functional map whenever a product changes. Ask whether the replacement covers the same jobs under the same conditions, whether its neighbors remain compatible, and whether documentation needs revision. Keep the map conceptual for learning; the professional drawing develops it into real circuits, ratings, and installation details. A clear function map makes that conversation faster and reduces the chance of buying a component that solves the wrong problem.

exercise.question: A kit includes PV modules, a solar charge controller, and a battery. Can you infer that it will supply ordinary AC appliances and automatically back up household circuits?
exercise.answer: No. The kit establishes some generation and storage functions, but AC conversion, distribution, transfer, controls, and the permitted installation remain to be demonstrated.
exercise.explanation: A complete system is defined by connected functions and supported operating modes. Component presence cannot substitute for the architecture or its installation evidence.

sections.title: Audit a service, not every nameplate in the house
paragraphs: A load audit translates everyday activities into electricity requirements. Begin with the decision it will support: annual bill reduction, evening battery dispatch, or specific outage service. A whole-house annual total and a selected-load overnight budget answer different questions. Copying every appliance rating into one list creates the appearance of precision while leaving usage, simultaneity, and priority unresolved.

Choose a recording period that includes the relevant habits. A weekday with nobody home may underrepresent cooking, laundry, cooling, or workshop use. Keep notes about weather and occupancy alongside the readings. The audit should explain why energy was used, because future changes in those activities alter the design assumptions. Write the service in plain language before choosing a measurement method.

figures.caption: Measure the load at a stated boundary, then preserve that boundary when comparing generation and storage.
figures.alt: Meters at array, inverter, battery, household load, and grid boundaries distinguish different electrical quantities.

sections.title: Separate three questions: energy, continuous power, and starts
paragraphs: Daily energy is the sum of consumption over a day, in kWh. Simultaneous power is the total demand from appliances operating together at a particular moment, in kW. Starting demand is a brief requirement when a motor or other device begins operating. An inverter may satisfy the energy-related average demand and still fail to start a required appliance.

Do not add every appliance's maximum rating and call it the ordinary household peak. Instead, identify plausible combinations and the essential circuit arrangement. At the same time, do not assume that low average consumption proves a small peak. A pump that runs only a few minutes per day can contribute little daily energy and still set a demanding power requirement. Obtain the exact appliance information or suitable professional measurements rather than applying an arbitrary surge multiplier.

figures.caption: Hypothetical load profiles can have the same 6 kWh energy but different peak power; size duration and instantaneous service separately.
figures.alt: Two hypothetical load rectangles illustrate equal energy with different power and duration.

sections.title: Measure operating patterns and preserve evidence
paragraphs: A plug-in energy meter can help with suitable plug-connected loads within its rating. Utility interval data can help describe whole-house usage patterns. Appliance documentation can provide rated quantities, but rated input is not the same as a measured daily total. Keep the source of each value: measured, documented, or assumed. This distinction tells the designer where more evidence will reduce uncertainty.

Cycling devices need observations over time. A refrigerator alternates among operating states, so multiplying one observed running wattage by twenty-four hours usually misrepresents its behavior. A device's standby consumption can matter because it persists. Record measurement duration, unit, mode, and conditions. Never open service equipment or create an unsafe measurement arrangement simply to improve a spreadsheet; the useful owner task is collecting accessible data and identifying where qualified measurement is needed.

sections.title: Work an essential-load energy budget
paragraphs: This hypothetical budget represents a mild-weather day with four selected loads. It intentionally uses assumed measured energy for the cycling refrigerator and simple power-times-duration arithmetic for the others. It excludes heating, cooling, cooking, water pumping, and inverter standby. Those exclusions are visible so another household cannot mistake this example for a universal emergency budget.

After adding the load energy, calculate the upstream storage requirement separately. A battery-to-AC efficiency assumption converts the service requirement to energy leaving the battery. Applying a usable operating window then converts that to nominal storage. Keeping these stages separate prevents the same loss from being applied twice and shows exactly which assumptions should be replaced by product data.

workedExample.title: One day's selected loads
givens: Refrigerator: assumed measured 1.10 kWh/day.
Router: 12 W for 24 h; lights: 30 W for 5 h; laptop: 45 W for 4 h.
Assumed battery-to-AC efficiency: 90%; operating window: 80% of nominal energy.
No PV contribution, standby, or other loads in this simplified example.
workedExample.result: The selected AC service uses about 1.72 kWh/day; the simplified nominal storage estimate is 2.39 kWh.
workedExample.discussion: These energy values do not establish the refrigerator's starting requirement or inverter compatibility. A measured start and the supported AC power envelope still need review.

sections.title: Turn the audit into a priority schedule
paragraphs: An essential load is a service you decide to preserve, not a universal appliance category. For one household, a communications device matters most; another has a water pump or accessibility equipment. Define priorities with the users. Some loads must remain automatic, some can be scheduled, and some can be omitted temporarily. The backup circuit design must reflect these choices rather than rely on somebody remembering to switch off everything else.

Scheduling affects simultaneous power and sometimes the value of solar self-consumption. Running a discretionary load at midday can use available generation, but only if it is practical and supported by the household routine. Do not make a fragile plan that depends on perfect behavior every day. Write which actions are automatic, which are manual, and what happens if the action is missed.

sections.title: Reconcile the list with a larger measurement boundary
paragraphs: Compare the itemized audit with utility or whole-house meter totals for the same dates. A discrepancy does not automatically mean a meter is wrong. The appliance list may exclude standby, lighting, cooling, pumps, or irregular use. The utility data may be interval averages at a different time boundary. Storage and generation can also affect what a utility import reading represents.

Use reconciliation to improve the audit instead of inventing a balancing appliance. Suppose listed uses add to 12 kWh while a matched whole-house reading is 18 kWh. The unexplained 6 kWh is a research task. Review dates and meter meaning, then look for omitted loads or faulty operating assumptions. A large remainder deserves explicit treatment before a battery or off-grid supply is sized from the smaller number.
sections.formula: Unexplained daily energy = matched total at the load boundary − itemized daily energy

sections.title: Keep a compact reference register
paragraphs: The table below separates evidence from inference. A recorded maximum can mean the highest sample in a dataset, a nameplate limit, or a measured starting event; these must not share an unlabeled column. Include both the confidence in the value and the consequence if it is wrong. A rough estimate for an optional lamp carries different design significance from an uncertain pump start.

Seasonal loads deserve their own scenarios. An annual average spreads winter heating or summer cooling across months when those loads may not operate. A backup brief should state the conditions it is intended to cover and the conditions outside it. For an independent system, poor-sun periods and recovery requirements can dominate even when the annual energy totals seem favorable.
rows: Refrigerator: 1.10 kWh, measured over stated dates
Captures cycling instead of assuming continuous operation
Documented or measured W and VA
Checks the relevant inverter surge envelope
Connects the design to household behavior

sections.title: Diagnose unrealistic budgets and test understanding
paragraphs: A budget often fails because a cycling load was treated as constant, a short high-power task was omitted, or a daily average replaced a peak. Another common error is calling a battery undersized when the real failure is an inverter or battery power limit. Compare the symptom with its timing: immediate shutdown at a start suggests a different constraint from gradual depletion after many hours.

Finish with a brief that another person can test. State the selected loads, assumed day or season, energy total, plausible simultaneous combinations, unresolved starting demands, and desired outage duration. Keep raw readings and notes. If the household later adds an electric vehicle, a heat pump, or a larger work schedule, update the audit before treating the original system forecast as a promise.

exercise.question: A 1,500 W kettle runs for six minutes, while a 20 W device runs for twenty-four hours. Which uses more daily energy, and which imposes greater running power?
exercise.answer: The 20 W device uses more energy: 0.48 kWh versus the kettle's 0.15 kWh. The kettle imposes greater running power.
exercise.explanation: Six minutes is 0.1 hour. The kettle consumes 1.5 × 0.1 = 0.15 kWh; the small device consumes 0.020 × 24 = 0.48 kWh. Energy importance and instantaneous power importance can point to different loads.

sources.label: NREL: PV and energy storage operation and maintenance, third edition

load-audit.outcome: Build a measured energy and power budget, distinguish operating demand from starting demand, and turn essential loads into a useful backup brief.

sections.title: Survey the constraints before placing modules
paragraphs: A site survey gathers the evidence that a catalog cannot supply. Two homes with identical annual electricity use may need different designs because their usable space, roof condition, shade, electrical service, and equipment locations differ. Start with a base sketch containing property boundaries, buildings, roof planes, obstacles, candidate equipment areas, and possible routes. Date every observation and note whether it came from a map, ground-level inspection, or professional assessment.

Separate measured facts from unresolved questions. A satellite image might suggest sufficient roof area while hiding a vent, an older addition, or a tree's seasonal shadow. A clean-looking roof does not reveal every structural detail. The survey becomes useful when it directs the next check: confirm dimensions, inspect condition, evaluate support, or establish a route. Its goal is a trustworthy design input rather than an impressive aerial rendering.

sections.title: Describe orientation with a consistent convention
paragraphs: Tilt is the angle of an array plane relative to horizontal. Azimuth describes its compass orientation using a stated convention. An array described merely as 'south-facing' is less useful than one with a measured or documented azimuth and tilt. In the PVWatts input convention, azimuth is expressed in degrees from north around the compass, so south is 180 degrees. Preserve the convention in the survey.

A preferred annual-production orientation is only one design consideration. Roof shape, shade, seasonal use, access, mounting feasibility, and the timing of consumption can matter. Compare candidate planes with the same production model instead of changing an orientation based on a slogan. A rooftop may have several planes that need separate inputs. Averaging their directions into one invented roof can obscure the very differences the survey is supposed to capture.

sections.title: Distinguish gross area from usable layout
paragraphs: Gross roof area is the geometric surface before constraints. Usable array area is what remains after actual obstacles, required access and setbacks, attachment feasibility, edge conditions, and layout rules have been reviewed. A ratio of roof area to module area is an early capacity screen; it is not a valid final module count. Module dimensions, gaps, and arrangement can waste otherwise available area.

Measure clear rectangles or polygons for each candidate plane and identify their boundaries. Keep chimneys, vents, skylights, drainage features, and access zones visible. Module placement also interacts with clamp zones, support geometry, and cable routing. The applicable local requirements and the exact mounting system determine some of these constraints. Do not import a setback dimension from an unrelated jurisdiction or product diagram.

sections.title: Work a simple rectangular-fit example
paragraphs: This example demonstrates geometry alone. It assumes the usable rectangle has already been determined by an appropriate review; it does not prescribe how to determine access clearances or structural requirements. The candidate module dimensions and gap are hypothetical. By comparing both orientations, the example shows why a surface-area quotient can be misleading.

Do not confuse portrait and landscape labels with electrical string arrangements. Rotating a module changes its footprint and may change permitted support details, but the electrical layout still needs its own design. If the geometric screen favors an orientation, check the module and mounting instructions before declaring the placement feasible. Real roofs often require a more detailed polygon layout than this teaching rectangle.

workedExample.title: Fit modules in an already-approved usable rectangle
givens: Hypothetical clear rectangle: 8.0 m wide × 4.0 m downslope.
Hypothetical module: 1.10 m × 1.80 m; gap between adjacent modules: 0.020 m.
No additional margins within this already-screened rectangle.
steps: Two portrait rows need 2 × 1.80 + 0.020 = 3.62 m, giving fourteen modules.
Three landscape rows need 3 × 1.10 + 2 × 0.020 = 3.34 m, giving twelve modules.
workedExample.result: The simple portrait layout fits fourteen modules; the simple landscape layout fits twelve.
workedExample.discussion: Area division gives 32 ÷ 1.98 ≈ sixteen module footprints before gaps, yet neither demonstrated arrangement fits sixteen. Geometry, margins, support, and obstacles must be evaluated explicitly.

sections.title: Follow the structural load path and roof condition
paragraphs: The load path is the chain by which forces reach a supporting structure. For a roof array it can pass from module to clamps, rails, attachments, framing, and the rest of the building. The survey should identify construction information and questions needed by the structural reviewer. Roof covering condition, remaining service life, prior damage, and planned replacement affect project sequencing as well as immediate feasibility.

An attachment is also a weatherproofing interface. The roof system and attachment family must work together under the specified instructions. Do not substitute a visible sealant bead for a documented attachment and flashing approach. A photograph can record what is visible; it cannot certify hidden framing or capacity. Keep professional findings and design revisions attached to the same site record so the electrical and mechanical teams use matching assumptions.

sections.title: Observe shade and the surrounding ground
paragraphs: Shade changes with solar position, season, and nearby objects. A single noon photograph cannot establish annual shading loss. Record obstruction locations and heights where practical, preserve dated views, and seek a method that resolves the relevant times and roof planes. Future tree growth, neighboring construction, and snow or debris accumulation belong among the uncertainties.

For a ground array, survey access, terrain, drainage, soil or foundation questions, vegetation, boundaries, and row spacing. More open sky does not eliminate mechanical design. A ground-mount product's capability must be interpreted through its documented design and site conditions. The survey should also consider how people will maintain vegetation and reach equipment after installation, because an inaccessible array can turn a small operational issue into a costly service visit.

sections.title: Map equipment positions and routes
paragraphs: A route is more than the straight-line distance between two boxes. It includes changes in elevation, entry points, permitted pathways, accessibility, environmental exposure, and installation details. Longer runs can affect cost and electrical loss. Battery and inverter locations require review of product clearances, environmental limits, and local requirements. Put candidate positions on the plan before a quotation treats them as settled.

Use the reference table to organize the handoff from survey to design. Mark each item as confirmed, provisional, or unresolved. An unresolved fact should have an owner and a next action. This makes later cost changes easier to understand: a quotation built on an unconfirmed service route carries a different uncertainty from one supported by a site visit.

sections.title: Diagnose survey shortcuts and review
paragraphs: The common shortcut is converting an attractive satellite view directly into a guaranteed panel count. Another is applying one annual shade percentage to every roof plane without evidence. Diagnose unexpected redesign by returning to the survey assumptions: was a dimension estimated, an obstacle missed, a route inaccessible, or a support requirement unknown? The lesson is to improve the evidence chain rather than merely reduce the module count until it fits.

A useful completed survey package contains a dated sketch, measurements with their methods, photographs, candidate layouts, structural and roof questions, shade observations, route assumptions, and local-review requirements. It remains a design input. The installed system must still receive the appropriate detailed design, permissions, inspection, and documentation.

exercise.answer: No. Twenty is only an area-based upper screen before constraints and layout.
exercise.explanation: Obstacles, access, setbacks, module geometry, gaps, attachment rules, and structural suitability can reduce the feasible count. A survey and reviewed layout are needed to turn area into an installable arrangement.

sections.title: Estimate energy over time, not a perfect moment
paragraphs: An array's nameplate capacity is a laboratory comparison of rated power. Production is energy delivered during a specified period. A 6 kW array does not produce 6 kWh in every daylight hour. Irradiance, orientation, temperature, shading, conversion, operating limits, and availability determine the changing output. Start by deciding whether the required result is monthly AC energy, hourly generation, or a seasonal estimate for another planning task.

An estimate is a model with inputs, a boundary, and uncertainty. A useful report lets someone reproduce the model and understand what it omits. 'About eight thousand units a year' is too vague: specify kWh, the year or weather basis, and whether the result is array DC or system AC. Production, utility export, and bill savings are different outputs and should not be combined into one unexplained headline.

sections.title: Irradiance and irradiation describe different things
paragraphs: Irradiance is instantaneous solar power per unit area, commonly W/m². Irradiation is solar energy per unit area over time, commonly kWh/m² for a stated period. Plane-of-array means the surface orientation of the actual modules. Horizontal resource data need an appropriate transformation before representing a tilted array. This is why location and orientation matter together.

Peak sun hours are an equivalent-energy shorthand. An assumed 4.5 kWh/m² daily irradiation corresponds to 4.5 hours at 1 kW/m², but does not claim there are exactly 4.5 clock hours of full-power operation. Dawn, clouds, and changing angles can deliver the same total through very different profiles. The shorthand is useful for transparent early arithmetic; a time-resolved model is better when timing or clipping matters.

sections.title: Use a documented model and keep its input record
paragraphs: PVWatts V8 documents inputs including DC system capacity, module category, array type, losses, location, tilt, azimuth, DC-to-AC ratio, and inverter efficiency. It reports monthly and annual AC energy and can provide hourly outputs. Keep the model version and weather-source identification with the result. These fields describe the model actually run rather than a generic production slogan.

For multiple substantially different roof planes, model the planes with their own orientations and assumptions before adding their energy. Keep weather and conventions consistent. If a detailed installation has unusual shade, storage controls, export limits, or availability issues, document whether the selected model represents them. A simpler model can still support early comparison when its omissions are visible, but it should not be presented as a complete dispatch or resilience simulation.

sections.title: Work a transparent early screening estimate
paragraphs: This calculation is intentionally a simplified screen and is not a PVWatts result. The assumed daily resource and retained-energy factor combine many effects into one visible multiplier. Real loss mechanisms do not necessarily scale identically each hour or season. The screen is useful because another person can follow the arithmetic and see why changing assumptions changes the conclusion.

Keep the output boundary explicit. The retained-energy factor here is assumed to convert the rated-capacity-times-resource estimate to delivered AC energy. If a later software result already reports AC energy after modeled conversion, do not apply this same factor again. That would lower the estimate twice for overlapping effects and make the comparison inconsistent.

workedExample.title: An early estimate for a hypothetical 6 kW array
givens: DC nameplate capacity: 6.0 kW.
Assumed average plane-of-array equivalent resource: 4.5 peak sun hours/day.
Assumed combined retained-energy factor to AC: 0.80; 365 days.
steps: Apply the assumed retained fraction: 27.0 × 0.80 = 21.6 kWh AC/day.
Specific yield = 7,884 ÷ 6.0 = 1,314 kWh per kW DC per year.
workedExample.result: The hypothetical annual screen is 7,884 kWh AC, or 1,314 kWh/kW DC/year.
workedExample.discussion: Specific yield compares energy per unit of installed DC capacity. It is a useful cross-check only when location, period, and output boundaries are understood. It is not a universal yield for a 6 kW system.

sections.formula: Screening energy = DC nameplate capacity × equivalent resource hours × assumed retained-energy fraction

sections.title: Losses are mechanisms, not one mystery percentage
paragraphs: Temperature changes module behavior; electrical mismatch can prevent all connected modules from operating at their individual best point; conductors and converters lose energy; soiling or shade reduce available input; downtime removes otherwise available production. A loss allowance should explain which of these effects it represents and what evidence supports it. Assigning a default to an unknown is acceptable for a screen only if the uncertainty remains visible.

Percentage losses combine multiplicatively when applied successively to the remaining energy. Two separate losses of 10% and 5% leave 0.90 × 0.95 = 0.855 of the starting quantity, a 14.5% total reduction. Simply adding them gives an approximation rather than the exact sequential result. More detailed models may calculate mechanisms directly, so copying those mechanisms into an additional catch-all factor can double count them.

sections.title: Recognize clipping, curtailment, and seasonal patterns
paragraphs: Clipping occurs when available DC power exceeds the inverter's permitted AC conversion output under the relevant conditions. Curtailment is a commanded reduction for another limit or operating instruction. Both can flatten output, but their causes differ. A DC array larger than the inverter AC rating is not automatically a design mistake; compare annual delivered energy and the documented operating envelope.

Monthly energy matters when consumption is seasonal. An annual surplus does not establish winter independence or overnight backup. Hourly generation is needed to explore self-consumption and interactions with a time-varying load. Keep storage energy balance separate from the generation model unless the tool explicitly models storage and its control strategy. A battery changes when energy is used; it does not increase the sunlight arriving at the array.

sections.title: Compare scenarios with a reference input table
paragraphs: A sensitivity study changes one or a small set of explained assumptions and records the difference. Compare orientation, shade allowance, array size, and inverter sizing deliberately. Do not change the weather basis, loss definitions, and DC capacity together and then attribute the entire difference to one product. Use an optimistic, central, and cautious scenario to show the decision's dependence on uncertainty.

The table below records what a future reviewer needs. For a real model, retain the exported input and output files as well as the summary. The estimate should have a review date and an explanation of assumptions that were chosen rather than measured. If a quotation's estimate cannot be reproduced, ask for these inputs before treating its annual energy as a performance promise.

sections.title: Diagnose an estimate and test understanding
paragraphs: An unexpectedly high estimate can come from the wrong capacity, an unshaded default, a location error, a mistaken orientation convention, or an omitted operating limit. An unexpectedly low estimate can come from duplicated loss factors or a mismatch between DC and AC boundaries. Before changing hardware, compare the input record and measurement definition.

During ownership, compare actual periods with modeled periods cautiously. Cloudy weather, downtime, changed shade, or data gaps can explain a difference without proving permanent degradation. Production estimates remain useful when updated with better evidence. The objective is a decision that survives honest uncertainty, not a precise-looking number that hides it.

exercise.answer: Not if the same inverter-conversion effect is already included.
exercise.explanation: The reported AC boundary already follows conversion. Applying the same efficiency again double counts that loss. An additional adjustment is appropriate only for a separate, explicitly omitted effect with a defensible basis.

sections.title: A shadow changes both the resource and the circuit
paragraphs: Shade first reduces the light reaching part of an array. That is an optical or irradiance effect. Electrical mismatch is a separate consequence: connected cells, modules, or strings may no longer share a compatible maximum-power operating point. Keeping the two effects distinct prevents the claim that a converter can recover all energy blocked by a tree. Electronics can change electrical operating conditions; they cannot restore light that never arrived.

Start with the physical shadow. Identify its source, movement, season, and the affected modules or cell groups. Then examine the electrical grouping. The same shaded area can lead to different electrical outcomes in different arrangements. A single annual shade percentage is a summary, not a complete explanation of the current-voltage behavior beneath it.

sections.title: Series and parallel impose shared quantities
paragraphs: In a series string, connected modules carry a common current. Parallel strings at a shared input operate at a common voltage. These circuit relationships explain mismatch: the chosen shared operating point cannot always coincide with every module's individual maximum-power point. Differences can arise from shade, temperature, manufacturing variation, degradation, or different wiring losses.

The familiar statement that one shaded module shuts down every module is too absolute. Actual behavior depends on shade geometry, module circuitry, bypass behavior, and conversion controls. Likewise, saying each module behaves independently merely because optimizers are present is too broad. Read the supported topology and operating limits. The useful question is how much additional electrical loss the chosen arrangement creates beyond the light already blocked.

sections.title: Read the datasheet before interpreting a shadow
paragraphs: Maximum-power voltage and current describe a useful operating point under stated conditions. Open-circuit voltage and short-circuit current describe boundary tests. Temperature coefficients describe how specified quantities change with cell temperature. Mechanical drawings, cell layout, and junction-box information can matter when predicting a narrow shadow's effect, but do not infer an undocumented bypass arrangement from a photograph of the front of a module.

Keep module variants separate. A product family can contain several wattages, dimensions, electrical characteristics, or connector options. Use the exact datasheet and instructions for the variant under consideration. A shade model based on the wrong cell grouping can produce a reassuring result without describing the installed product. A beginner's screening estimate should say explicitly when it treats shade as a uniform reduction rather than resolving the detailed circuitry.

sections.title: Compare energy consequences with a simple example
paragraphs: The following example is a teaching comparison rather than a prediction of any brand. It starts with an assumed unshaded daily energy and separates missing light from additional mismatch. The electronics scenario changes only the extra electrical loss. Both cases still suffer the same optical loss because the obstruction remains.

This distinction is useful in a quotation. Ask whether the claimed gain comes from measured or modeled shade conditions, reduced mismatch, a changed layout, or an assumed generic percentage. Recoverable mismatch cannot exceed the mismatch that existed. If the estimate appears to restore all shaded irradiance, ask the designer to show the energy accounting.

workedExample.title: Optical loss remains after electrical mitigation
givens: Hypothetical unshaded daily output: 20 kWh at a common comparison boundary.
Assumed shade reduces the available energy by 15%.
Case A has an additional 8% electrical mismatch loss on the remaining energy.
Case B reduces that additional mismatch to an assumed 3%; all other effects unchanged.
steps: Difference: 16.49 − 15.64 = 0.85 kWh, approximately 5.4% of Case A.
workedExample.result: The hypothetical electrical mitigation recovers 0.85 kWh, while the 3 kWh optical loss remains.
workedExample.discussion: The chosen loss percentages are illustrative, not measured product performance. A real comparison needs a validated shade model and documented conversion behavior.

sections.title: Understand what module-level conversion changes
paragraphs: A microinverter converts a module's DC output to AC at that module. A power optimizer typically performs module-level DC conversion within a compatible architecture. Their operating boundaries and controls differ. DOE describes module-level conversion as allowing more independent operation than a shared string conversion arrangement, but the exact installation still has input ranges, power limits, wiring requirements, and compatibility constraints.

Evaluate the complete design. Different roof orientations may be separated across MPPT inputs or handled through a supported module-level arrangement. Shade mitigation may introduce additional rooftop devices and service considerations. Compare delivered energy, supported behavior, warranty scope, and access. Do not treat the technology category as a guarantee of a fixed percentage improvement, universal shade immunity, or compatibility with an arbitrary battery system.

sections.title: Turn observations into a useful shade assessment
paragraphs: A shade assessment should preserve the obstruction geometry and the time pattern behind its result. Record tree or building locations, roof planes, and the method used. Leaf-on and leaf-off conditions can differ. A chimney's shadow crosses different modules as the sun moves. Snow, soiling, and nearby reflective surfaces should not be casually folded into an unexplained shade allowance.

Test alternatives that change the cause. Removing a shaded module location, shifting a layout, separating orientations, or choosing another site can outperform adding electronics to a poor placement. Keep legal, practical, and ongoing maintenance constraints visible when tree management is proposed. If a tree is expected to grow back into the relevant sky area, the comparison should not assume a permanent shade-free result without an upkeep plan.

sections.title: Use the reference table to separate evidence
paragraphs: A useful review compares mechanisms and evidence instead of slogans. The reference table shows how the same word 'loss' can hide different questions. Preserve the original model assumptions and the array grouping so an annual loss estimate can be investigated later. A production chart without the corresponding layout is much harder to interpret.

Mismatch can also arise after installation. A damaged module, changed vegetation, altered string grouping, or degraded connection may change performance. Monitoring can reveal a recurring pattern, but a chart alone cannot uniquely identify the fault. Report the time and conditions of a suspected issue and let qualified service personnel perform any necessary electrical or physical investigation.

sections.title: Diagnose overconfident claims and review
paragraphs: The common mistakes are using a noon photograph as an annual shade assessment, multiplying a shaded-area fraction directly into energy without considering timing, and promising that optimizers recover sunlight. Another error is treating a shade estimate as a production guarantee. Its confidence depends on the site evidence, model assumptions, and stability of the surroundings.

When reviewing a claim, ask for the before-and-after layout, a common energy boundary, and the model's separate loss assumptions. If an improvement remains useful in a cautious shade scenario, it is a stronger planning result than an impressive central estimate alone. The goal is to choose an arrangement whose benefits can be explained and whose future changes can be diagnosed.

exercise.explanation: The original retained fraction is 0.88 × 0.95 = 0.836. Eliminating only mismatch raises it to 0.88. The obstruction's lost irradiance remains, and the percentages are illustrative rather than a product guarantee.

sections.title: Module watts are the start of the specification
paragraphs: A module label gives rated electrical quantities under stated conditions. Maximum-power rating is useful for comparing capacity and calculating an array's nominal DC size. It does not establish compatibility by itself. The designer also needs open-circuit voltage, short-circuit current, maximum-power voltage and current, temperature coefficients, permitted protection, dimensions, and installation requirements.

A string is modules connected in series. An array can contain one or several strings connected through a supported topology. Think of a string as a coordinated operating group rather than simply a row on the roof. Physical rows, roof planes, and electrical strings need not correspond one-to-one. Preserve both the placement drawing and the electrical grouping to understand the installed system.

sections.title: Series adds voltage; parallel adds current
paragraphs: For identical modules under the same conditions, series connection adds their voltage while the string current is shared. Parallel identical strings add current while their operating voltage is shared. These arithmetic relationships provide an initial screen. They do not ensure that dissimilar modules all reach their independent maximum power, because the shared quantities constrain their operating points.

Use like quantities when adding. A string's open-circuit voltage is built from module Voc values at the relevant temperature, not from Vmp. A maximum-power current comparison uses Imp under the relevant conditions, while input short-circuit limits need Isc and the required treatment. Mixing test boundaries is one of the easiest ways to create a plausible but invalid string worksheet.

sections.title: The I-V curve explains why the nameplate is not a fixed source
paragraphs: A module operates somewhere along a current-voltage curve determined by conditions. At open circuit, current delivered to the external load is zero; at short circuit, terminal voltage is near zero. Useful power lies between these boundaries, and the maximum-power point is where voltage times current is greatest. An MPPT seeks a suitable operating point through its control behavior.

Available current responds strongly to irradiance, while temperature changes the voltage envelope as well as output. Cell temperature differs from outdoor air temperature. A string that appears suitable using room-temperature voltage may exceed an input maximum in cold conditions or fall outside the useful tracking range in hot conditions. Both limits deserve examination, even though they occur at different times.

sections.title: Work a cold-voltage screening example
paragraphs: The following values describe a hypothetical module, not a real manufacturer's datasheet. The coefficient is expressed as percent per degree Celsius; it is converted to a decimal fraction before multiplication. The assumed minimum cell temperature is a design input for this example rather than a climate claim. Actual design uses the applicable temperature method and the exact documentation.

Compare the calculated value with the equipment's absolute PV voltage limit rather than relying on power clipping. An input can limit excess power only under its permitted operating conditions; that does not authorize excess voltage. Leave required design margins and corrections to the documented system method. This arithmetic example only demonstrates why adding one more module can reverse a compatibility screen.

workedExample.title: Three or four hypothetical modules in series?
givens: Module Voc at 25°C: 40.0 V; Voc coefficient: −0.28%/°C.
Assumed minimum cell temperature: −10°C.
Illustrative equipment maximum PV Voc: 150 V; no additional correction in this teaching calculation.
workedExample.result: Three modules pass this simplified voltage screen; four exceed the illustrative 150 V maximum.
workedExample.discussion: Passing this one screen does not establish a permissible installation. Check tracking and startup range, hot voltage, current, protection, and the manufacturer's complete requirements.

sections.title: Read a real controller's numbers at the correct side
paragraphs: The Victron SmartSolar MPPT 150/35 manual lists a 150 V maximum PV open-circuit voltage, 35 A maximum PV short-circuit current, and 35 A maximum battery current. Although two figures share a numerical value, they describe different limits. The manual also distinguishes startup and continued-operation voltage relative to battery voltage. Read the notes beside the table; headings alone do not carry every condition.

Use this real manual as a model for evidence collection, not as permission to attach the hypothetical string above. The real system still needs the correct module data and installation design. The controller is a battery charger rather than an AC grid inverter. A 35 A battery-side output does not mean every PV arrangement with an operating current below 35 A is acceptable.

sections.title: Check parallel current and protection separately
paragraphs: Adding a parallel string increases available current at a shared voltage. Two identical strings with an assumed Imp of 10 A each have an ideal combined maximum-power current of 20 A under the same conditions. Their combined Isc must be assessed separately. Operating current limits and short-circuit limits serve different checks, and the applicable design treatment may include additional factors.

Parallel paths also change possible reverse-current and protection considerations. The module's allowed series protection, the number of source paths, device ratings, conductors, connectors, and equipment instructions matter. A connector that mates physically is not proof of an approved pairing. Keep this chapter's arithmetic separate from fuse selection and field connection work; those require the complete documented circuit and qualified installation.

sections.title: Maintain a string reference worksheet
paragraphs: A worksheet should show the exact module variant and every checked equipment input. If an inverter has multiple independent MPPT inputs, do not casually combine their current allowances into a single input limit. Record which strings land on which tracker and whether inputs are actually independent. A marketing phrase such as 'dual input' can describe a physical connector arrangement without answering all tracking questions.

The table below creates a traceable chain from module label to array arrangement. Record the source document revision and design assumptions beside each final calculation. When a supplier changes the module variant, rerun the worksheet instead of assuming the same wattage means the same voltage and current. Small datasheet differences can matter at an operating boundary.

sections.title: Diagnose string mistakes and review
paragraphs: Common mistakes include increasing series count until the watts fit without checking cold voltage, mixing orientations under one shared tracker without review, and treating every current number as the same limit. Another is assuming an oversized array is always safe because the converter clips. Power, voltage, current, temperature, and topology are separate constraints.

Before purchasing, make the string arrangement reviewable as a drawing and a calculation sheet. Mark each limit's source and every unresolved assumption. A sound preliminary screen should identify why a configuration remains a candidate, which checks it has passed, and which installation requirements remain. It should never turn a partial arithmetic result into a complete wiring instruction.

sections.title: Compatibility is a set of interfaces
paragraphs: Two products are compatible when their connected functions operate within supported conditions. Matching a nominal voltage or connector shape is only a preliminary observation. A complete screen includes electrical ranges, continuous and temporary limits, control permissions, communications, environmental conditions, mechanical installation, and the intended operating modes.

Build an interface matrix before ranking price. Give every connection a row: modules to tracker, battery to converter, converter to AC service, control device to battery, module to mounting, and meters to monitoring. Add the exact product model and variant at each end. The matrix should contain evidence rather than a confidence adjective such as 'should work.' Unsupported assumptions are visible tasks to resolve before purchase.

figures.caption: The compatibility review follows every electrical and control interface in the chosen architecture.
figures.alt: Conceptual module conversion and battery paths show where different equipment interfaces must agree.

sections.title: Compare operating envelopes, not one nominal point
paragraphs: An operating envelope is the permitted range of conditions. For PV inputs it can include maximum open-circuit voltage, tracking range, startup requirements, input current, short-circuit current, and allowed power treatment. For battery interfaces it includes voltage during charging and discharge as well as current and power limits. A nominal 48 V label does not prove the entire actual battery range lies inside an inverter's input envelope.

Distinguish absolute limits from controlled performance limits. An inverter may cap power under supported circumstances. It cannot be assumed to tolerate an excessive absolute voltage because it has clipping behavior. A preliminary compatibility matrix should name which kind of limit is being checked and preserve the manufacturer's conditions. Borderline values warrant a documented design decision rather than an optimistic rounding choice.

sections.title: Learn the method from a real specification table
paragraphs: The Victron SmartSolar MPPT 150/35 and 150/45 specification table identifies 150 V maximum PV open-circuit voltage for both models, while battery-current limits differ at 35 A and 45 A. It also lists maximum PV short-circuit current separately. This is a useful example of why a product-family name and an output rating do not replace input review.

The lesson is methodological: read the headings and footnotes, then compare the exact model. Do not transfer an allowance from the 150/45 to the 150/35, from one battery-voltage configuration to another, or from a charger to a grid inverter. Save the document revision and any manufacturer clarification with the candidate list. Product-specific permission must remain tied to the actual product.

sections.title: Work a hypothetical power-interface screen
paragraphs: The following example uses imagined ratings and is not an approved equipment pairing. It separates load delivery from battery-terminal demand. A battery's energy capacity could easily be large enough for the requested duration while its continuous current limit remains inadequate. The lowest operating voltage is relevant because current rises as voltage falls for the same input power.

Apply the same reasoning to every bottleneck. The converter's continuous AC rating, battery current allowance, cable and protection design, and environmental derating may all constrain the result. The example's calculation is only one row in the matrix. A positive result would not settle communications, motor starts, transfer capability, or the manufacturer's supported battery list.

workedExample.title: Does the battery continuous-current limit support the load?
givens: Hypothetical AC demand: 3,000 W continuously.
Assumed conversion efficiency for screening: 92%.
Hypothetical minimum battery operating voltage: 44 V.
Hypothetical battery continuous-discharge limit: 60 A.
steps: Compare 74.1 A with the stated 60 A continuous limit.
Equivalent simplified AC power at the limit = 44 × 60 × 0.92 = 2,428.8 W.
workedExample.result: The imagined battery fails this continuous-current screen for a 3 kW AC load.
workedExample.discussion: Increasing nominal kWh without increasing the supported discharge capability would not resolve the bottleneck. Real efficiency, operating limits, and allowable architecture must come from exact documentation.

sections.title: Control compatibility can decide whether energy flows
paragraphs: A BMS may request reduced charging or prohibit discharge under specified conditions. A supported system must communicate or enforce those permissions in the intended manner. CAN, an RJ45-shaped connector, or a shared brand name is not sufficient evidence of the required protocol, pinout, settings, and firmware support. Control wiring deserves its own row in the matrix.

Distinguish a monitoring connection from a control connection. A dashboard may read a battery value without having the authority or mechanism to enforce its operating permissions. Document what happens when communications are lost. If that behavior is unknown, the candidate remains unresolved. Do not improvise a cable or defeat a permission merely to make two attractive components appear compatible.

sections.title: Grid and backup modes need their own proof
paragraphs: Grid-connected operation, export limitation, charging from the grid, and isolated backup are different modes. A product may support some and not others, or support them only with additional equipment and approved configurations. DOE's explanation of grid-following and grid-forming functions helps distinguish conversion from the ability to establish an isolated supply.

List the intended service conditions: supply voltage and frequency, supported circuit arrangement, required simultaneous loads, outage transfer behavior, solar behavior during isolation, and restart after depletion. A whole-home marketing description should be converted into a documented supported-load and transfer design. Utility approval and local acceptance concern the complete installation, not merely the presence of a certification logo on one component.

sections.title: Reference table: capture the evidence chain
paragraphs: Compatibility evidence has a hierarchy of usefulness. Exact current manufacturer instructions and supported configurations are more relevant than a reseller's short description. A verified manufacturer clarification can resolve an ambiguity; an anecdotal forum success does not establish permission for another configuration. Keep model variants, revisions, firmware, and settings in the record.

Mechanical and environmental limits belong beside the electrical ones. Module clamps, equipment clearances, terminal conductor acceptance, weather exposure, temperature, and access can disqualify an otherwise promising pair. The table is intended to organize review, not replace the engineer or installer. It should make unresolved facts easy to see rather than bury them inside a single compatibility score.

sections.title: Diagnose mismatched packages and review
paragraphs: The usual compatibility failure begins with a shortcut: nominal voltage replaces a range, peak power replaces continuous power, a family manual replaces the exact variant, or a physically fitting plug replaces protocol evidence. Another mistake is accepting substitutions without rerunning the matrix. A replacement module or battery can change a previously resolved interface.

Finish the shortlist with explicit states: confirmed from identified evidence, provisional pending a named check, or rejected with the limiting reason. Keep purchase decisions attached to these states. A compatible plan should be understandable to a reviewer who did not participate in the shopping process, and the installation record should preserve the pairing actually built.

exercise.question: Two batteries each advertise 5 kWh, but one supports an assumed 2 kW continuous discharge and the other 4 kW. Are they equivalent for a 3 kW backup load?
exercise.answer: No. Under those stated assumptions, the 2 kW unit fails the continuous-power requirement, while the 4 kW unit remains a candidate.
exercise.explanation: Energy capacity concerns duration; discharge power concerns how rapidly energy can be delivered. The second unit still needs voltage, control, conversion, starting, and installation compatibility checks.
